metadata.description: Ringleader Azure onboarding: the OPTIONAL network landing pad (vnet + workstations subnet + NAT gateway + NSG). Deploy at RESOURCE GROUP scope, after azuredeploy.json. Separate from azuredeploy.json on purpose: that file is also deployed by the Terraform module, which compares Azure's normalized echo of it against the file on every plan, so it may carry no outputs block and no parameter default it does not pass. This template is deployed only by az, so it is free to have both.
Prefix for the created resources (vnet, NSG, NAT gateway, public IP). Change it if those names are already taken in this resource group.
Region for the landing pad. Defaults to the resource group's.

Which /16 this region's landing pad takes: the VNet gets 10.(70 + regionIndex).0.0/16 and every subnet below is carved out of it. REQUIRED -- there is deliberately no default, because nothing here can tell a first region from a second and a default would hand the second one the first one's range in silence. An Azure VNet is regional, so a second region is a second VNet, and two VNets on one range can never be peered; the only remedy is to renumber and re-onboard. Give your FIRST region 0 -- that is 10.70.0.0/16, the range this template has always created, so an existing deployment is unchanged -- and the next region 1. Never reuse an index. Past ten regions, or on your own IPAM, set vnetCidr instead.

Optional override for the VNet address space. Empty -- the default -- derives it from regionIndex, which is what keeps two regions apart. Set it to bring your own range, and then the three subnets below follow it and keeping your regions distinct is yours to do.
Optional override for the workstations subnet. Empty derives the second /24 of the VNet range (10.70.1.0/24 at index 0), so there is no second value to keep in step when the VNet moves.

A single CIDR allowed inbound on TCP 22. Empty (the default) adds NO inbound rule, which leaves workstations unreachable from outside the VNet -- correct only if you reach it privately (VPN / ExpressRoute / peering). Ringleader ships no bastion and no SSH tunnel: rl shell, tmux, port-forwards and VS Code Web all dial the workstation on 22.

Optional, and empty opens nothing. A single CIDR allowed inbound on the secondary SSH port (TCP 2222). Some Ringleader workstation types run their own SSH daemon on that port inside the VM, beside the VM's own sshd on 22, and rl shell dials it instead of 22 for those; others never use it. An NSG covers the whole subnet, so this admits the port to every VM on it.

Reserve an empty subnet for the egress gateway VM that Ringleader's hostname-level egress control uses. On by default. Ringleader builds that VM here once you declare a policy naming hostnames, and it is billed; carving the range now means the NSG rules that permit workstation -> gateway traffic can name one stable prefix, and avoids renumbering later. Hand its id back as spec.subnet on the EgressGateway -- no gateway VM is built until you do. Azure does not bill for the subnet, so leaving it on costs nothing until a policy builds the VM; the VM itself then carries a standalone public IP, billed separately.

Optional override for the gateway subnet. Empty derives the 241st /24 of the VNet range (10.70.240.0/24 at index 0), which sits well clear of the workstations subnet so growing that one later does not collide. Set it only to override, and then it must sit inside the VNet range.

Reserve a second subnet -- the one you put the WORKSTATIONS a gateway governs in. On by default. A gateway steers a whole subnet and serves only the boxes it holds a policy for, so a steered subnet must hold governed boxes and nothing else; the workstations subnet is where every workstation in the VNet goes, governed or not. It carries the same NSG as the workstations subnet, so rl shell still reaches a box in it, and NEITHER a route table NOR the NAT gateway: Ringleader claims the subnet by putting its own UDR on it and declines one that already references a route table, and a governed box's egress is meant to be its gateway's. Azure does not bill for a subnet.

Optional override for the governed subnet. Empty derives the 15th /20 of the VNet range (10.70.224.0/20 at index 0), immediately below the gateway /24 at the top of the VNet, so the two egress-control ranges stay together and the workstations prefix is free to grow. Set it only to override, and then it must sit inside the VNet range.

variables.effectiveSubnets: [concat(variables('workstationSubnets'), if(parameters('createGatewaySubnet'), variables('gatewaySubnets'), createArray()), if(parameters('createGovernedSubnet'), variables('governedSubnets'), createArray()))]

resources.comments: The egress gateway subnet's own security group. Azure's default rules are rules INSIDE a group, so a subnet and a NIC with none are not filtered at all -- and the gateway VM Ringleader builds here carries a standalone PUBLIC IP, which without this would put the proxy's listeners and its sshd on the internet. THE ONE RULE IS NOT OPTIONAL, and the defaults are not a substitute for it: AllowVnetInBound at 65000 is source VirtualNetwork to DESTINATION VirtualNetwork, while a steered packet arrives addressed to the PUBLIC host the workstation was reaching -- a UDR next hop does not rewrite the destination -- so it would miss that rule, fall to DenyAllInBound at 65500, and every governed box would lose the internet while the gateway stayed healthy. Allowing the VNet inbound to ANY destination is what Ringleader also writes on the VM's own NIC (azgateway's gatewayNSGRule); this group is the second layer and the two must agree. Outbound is untouched, so the gateway keeps the internet access it exists to police.
resources.name: [variables('gatewayNsgName')]

metadata.description: The subnet for the workstations a gateway governs, or empty if createGovernedSubnet was false. Hand it back as providerConfig.azure.subnetId on the workstations that carry an egress policy.

The subnet the egress gateway VM runs in, or empty if createGatewaySubnet was false. Hand it back as spec.subnet on the EgressGateway -- Ringleader builds no gateway until you do, because a gateway placed in the subnet it steers routes its own egress into itself. NOT governedSubnetId, which is the workstations'.
